findings.reason: naming the body extent as the parser record rather than a second regex removes the one boundary derivation §16 leaves un-owned, so the moved `section_prose` does not fork span detection the parser already owns.
findings.text: §16 states the moved reader derives its headings and spans "from one pass over the parser's record set", yet the slicer it moves still computes the document `<body>`/`</body>` extent with its own two regexes, and the plan assigns that boundary no owner; the parser already carries a `body` structural record (`reckon/_plan_html.py:196`)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the one public addition, `section_prose` on `reckon/_plan_html.py`, hides body-span clamping, heading identity, landed-card interiors, skip-tag removal and entity decoding behind an ordered sequence of (identity, prose) slices, consumed by the digests, the search text, the section response and the dispatch brief. Substantial behaviour behind a small interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the document-body extent has no owner in the moved design; see FINDING duplicate_owner below.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23. §16 names its one net public addition (`section_prose`) and what it retires (the interim public `strip_tags` at `reckon/_plan_html.py:1880` becomes private `_strip_tags`), and states why the moved `section_record_id`/`section_anchor`/`DOCUMENT_UNIT` are moves the family does not count — verified against `reckon/interface_counts.py:74` (`definitions` yields only FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/ClassDef, so module-level constants are not counted). §20 adds no public definition and says so.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16 runs a lexical census over the codebase (`grep -rn 'stripped_strings\|get_text(' reck/`, fourteen lines), names the shared owners it will reuse (`_TAG_RE` and `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` on `reckon/_plan_html.py:1876-1877`, `section_record_id` on the same module, `structured_section_spans` at `reckon/_plan_html.py:415`, the public readers `roadmap.implementable_sections` at `reckon/roadmap.py:107` and `list_plan_reviews`), and classifies every remaining extractor by kind rather than proposing new machinery beside it. All named owners were verified to exist.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two candidates are justified in-text: `_strip_tags` is not a bare `_TAG_RE` substitution but adds `html.unescape` and removal of the `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` interiors (the same reason `count_open_decisions` at `reckon/_plan_html.py:1909` keeps the bare form), and §16 states why the coverage predicate cannot be a call to `read_plan_review` (one-record join vs. set join). The interim `_prose_slices` is deleted rather than left as a delegator to the new reader.
